overview.description: Jhyap (also known as Yaniv or Dhumbal) is a draw-and-discard game from Nepal that has gained international popularity. Players aim to have the lowest total card value in their hand by forming sets and runs that can be discarded. When a player thinks they have the lowest hand, they call 'Jhyap' to end the round.
overview.originName: Jhyap (झ्याप) or Dhumbal (धुम्बल) in Nepal; Yaniv (יניב) in Israel

history.origins: Jhyap originated in Nepal, where it is known by this name (meaning 'intoxicated' or 'high' in slang). The game spread to Israel around the beginning of the 21st century, where it became known as Yaniv (a Hebrew personal name). It has since spread to other countries including the Netherlands (where it's called Kluft).
timeline: Traditional: Played in Nepal as Jhyap/Dhumbal
Early 2000s: Gains popularity in Israel as Yaniv
Present day: Popular in Nepal, Israel, and among backpackers worldwide
history.evolution: The game evolved from traditional rummy-style games but with a unique mechanism: instead of melding cards to the table, players discard sets and runs, and one of the discarded cards can be picked up by the next player. The 'call' mechanism to end play is also distinctive.
history.cultural: In Nepal, the game is traditionally played counter-clockwise and is a popular social game. In Israel, it became extremely popular among young people and travelers. The game is often played for small stakes or just for fun. The penalty for a wrong call (Asaf in Israel) adds excitement.

rules.objective: Have the lowest total value of cards in your hand. Form sets (three or four of a kind) and runs (three or more consecutive cards of the same suit) to discard cards. Call 'Jhyap' when you think you have the lowest hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. Each player is dealt 5 cards
2. One card is turned face-up to start the discard pile
3. Players take turns: a. Discard one or more cards as a valid set or run b. Draw one card (from the draw pile or the discard pile)
4. Sets and runs are placed on the discard pile, not the table
5. The next player may take any one card from the discarded set/run
6. When a player thinks their hand total is low enough (typically 5 or less), they call 'Jhyap' instead of taking a turn
7. All players reveal their hands
8. If the caller has the lowest (or tied for lowest) total, they score 0 and others score their hand values
9. If another player has a lower total, the caller scores their hand value plus a penalty (usually 30), and others score their hand values
10. Play continues until a player reaches the elimination threshold (usually 200 points)
keyRules: Must discard before drawing (unlike most rummy games)
Can only discard valid sets (3-4 of a kind) or runs (3+ consecutive same suit)
Next player can take any one card from a discarded set/run
Can call 'Jhyap' only at the start of your turn, before discarding
If hand value is 5 or less, you can call Jhyap (threshold varies by group)
Ties go to the caller (caller wins ties)

strategy.basic: Form sets and runs quickly to reduce hand value. Call Jhyap when your hand is low (5 or less). Pick up cards that help complete your combinations.
strategy.intermediate: Watch what cards opponents discard to deduce their hands. Consider the risk before calling Jhyap - if wrong, you get a 30-point penalty. Sometimes it's better to play safe and not call.
strategy.advanced: Bluff by discarding cards that make opponents think your hand is stronger or weaker than it is. Calculate probabilities of opponents' hand values based on discards. Time your calls based on opponents' tendencies.
tips: Keep your hand flexible - don't commit to one combination too early
Jokers are valuable (worth 0) - save them for emergencies
Watch which cards opponents pick up from discards
Don't call Jhyap with exactly 5 if opponents seem to have low hands too
Remember which cards have been played
Sometimes it's worth picking up a high card to complete a run

list.name: Kluft
list.description: Dutch variant: only the top card of the discard pile may be taken; jokers are not wild (value zero only); player calls 'Kluft' with 5 or fewer points; others may challenge with 'Onderkluft' claiming a lower hand (4 or less); penalty 15 for unsuccessful challengers; elimination at 100; exactly 100 reduces to 50.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Override values for penalty and elimination threshold not mapped to engine.constants in this schema.

list.name: Nepal standard
list.description: Play is counter-clockwise. Often played with 52 cards and no jokers; Jacks score 0, Queens and Kings 10. Next player may take any card from the previous discard (not only first or last). Wrong-call penalty 25 (not 30); other players do not score their hand on wrong call. Elimination at 100 points; no score reductions at 50/100/200.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Deck and penalty differences not expressed as engine.constants overrides.

list.name: Call threshold variants
list.description: Some play Yaniv/Jhyap can be called with 6 or fewer points, or 7, 10, 11, or 13. No limit is possible with a rule that play cannot end before everyone has had one turn.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Call threshold is rule text; no engine.constants path for this.

list.name: Score reduction variants
list.description: Israeli variants: hitting 200 exactly may reduce to 150 (not 100); or any multiple of 50 (50,100,150,200) reduces by 50; or score halved at 100, 150, or 200 exactly. Three successful Yanivs in a game may deduct 20 points (suspended with two players left).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Score reduction rules are gameplay variants; no engine.constants override for these.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card pack plus two jokers; five cards each; draw-and-discard to form sets and runs; call Jhyap when lowest hand (Pagat Yaniv).
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades); suits matter for runs only; jokers are wild; face values for penalty points.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks; number cards count face value (e.g. 10=10), face cards often 10 each; aces 1 or 11 by variant; lowest hand calls to end round.

hero.tagline: Discard smart. Call at the right moment. Lowest hand wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Nepali draw-and-discard game (also known as Yaniv in Israel) where players minimize their hand value by discarding sets and runs, then call when ready.

prompts.human: Jhyap (Yaniv): Each player gets 5 cards. Your goal is to get the lowest hand value. Discard sets (e.g., three 7s) or runs (e.g., 4-5-6) and draw replacements. When your hand is low enough, call 'Jhyap' to end the round. Lowest hand wins.
prompts.ai: Game: Jhyap (Yaniv/Dhumbal). 2-5 players, 54-card deck (52+2 jokers). Deal 5 cards each. Gameplay: Players take turns discarding sets (identical ranks) or runs (consecutive ranks same suit) to discard pile, then draw from deck. Call Jhyap when hand value is low to trigger showdown. Scoring: Number cards=face value, J/Q/K=10, Joker=25. Lowest hand value wins round. Multiple rounds until player reaches target score.

scoring.description: Points based on hand value. Discard to minimize. Call Jhyap when low.
scoring.winCondition: The object is to score as few points as possible, and in particular to keep your cumulative total below 200.
